title: A new thought can wait
meaning: You can freely introduce an unfamiliar subject, make your words clear and still leave room for an emotional answer that has not yet taken shape.
text: An unexpected turn in conversation does not always receive an immediate answer. On your Vishuddha, Justice in the physical position supports precise questions about what was said. The Fool in energy encourages you to open a subject without a ready script, allowing the first response to be unexpected. The Hanged Man in emotions brings a sense of suspension: the familiar view has shifted, while a new one is not yet clear. You can understand the proposal while your feeling about it is still changing.

Suppose you suggest spending an evening telling each other about something you do not usually discuss. The question “Does it have to be a secret?” clarifies the idea: this is an invitation to a new conversation, rather than a demand for confessions. **An unexpected subject does not require a quick answer**. After clarification, you may still not know whether the idea appeals. This pause concerns the experience of the suggestion; it need not mean refusing conversation or being unwilling to hear each other.

The difficulty appears if you expect a precise explanation to remove the hesitation immediately. Repeated questions then start demanding a settled feeling: “You understand now, so why are you quiet?” Openness to the conversation remains when clarity of meaning does not dictate the speed of response. A proposal can be understood and still need another perspective before you both find your words.
